summary_for_principal:
This closes the last open sub-part of the current checklist item, and with it, the entire original 8-item checklist.

One more setting the system accepts but never acts on: a loop can declare that taking it should make some earlier work stop counting, so later steps don't read superseded results. Nothing in the system ever reads that declaration — it's silently ignored.

Before fixing this, I re-checked a claim carried over from earlier work: that the reference example already relies on this setting, ruling out a simple refusal. That claim was false — repeated, unchecked, across several earlier write-ups. The real example doesn't use it; only this system's own instructions document did, in one illustrative snippet, now corrected.

Refused it cleanly, matching how similar gaps this session were handled: authors are told plainly it isn't supported, rather than having their instruction silently dropped. Also found and fixed a real, separate bug in how a loop decision is replayed on a later call.

Full test suite: 389 passed, 6 new.

Numbered actions:
1. Nothing needs deciding right now.
2. This closes the original 8-item checklist in full.

decisions.problem: invalidates is accepted by the schema and model (RouteTarget.invalidates/RouteOption.invalidates) but never read anywhere the engine resolves state. options_rejected: Implement invalidates for real, marking a named node's recorded outputs as superseded: rejected for this pass — the spec names no mechanism for 'a superseded output' (error? absent? a sentinel?), and doing this correctly means new state-tracking machinery in exactly the replay-position territory that produced D19-D23/D27 and the _advance_route bug found while investigating this item; a hasty implementation risks adding a sixth bug to that class rather than closing one.

Leave it silently unread, as found: rejected — a definition author who declares invalidates is expressing an intent the engine would otherwise ignore without ever telling them, exactly the silent-gap shape CLAUDE.md's 'fail closed' principle refuses.
